contract.proves:
PUBLISHED must mean installable from every node, not from the node that
happened to handle the upload.

THE PROBLEM. The manifest authority is cluster-wide but the blob store is
per-node: a publish materializes bytes only in the local CAS of the instance
that received them. Every other node reads the same manifest, reports the
artifact as PUBLISHED, and cannot serve it. Nothing re-ran the seeder to fix
this, because seeding was a one-shot startup goroutine — so the gap persisted
until that node's repository happened to restart.

Observed 2026-08-16: cluster-controller@1.2.317's blob existed only on
globule-ryzen and ai-memory@1.2.317's only on globule-dell. The remaining
nodes raised repository.identity.missing_blob_for_published_manifest as an
ERROR while the staged archives that would have healed them sat unused in
/var/lib/globular/packages/ on those same nodes. An install routed to any of
them failed on an artifact the cluster insisted was published.

This is the single largest contributor to the deploy pipeline failing about
half the time: whether a deploy worked depended on which repository instance
served the install, which is not something the operator controls or can see.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS FORBIDDEN. Healing package bytes from the MinIO mirror
is ruled out (heal_published_artifacts_from_minio_mirror,
repository.minio_is_not_valid_package_source) — packages do not live in
MinIO. The only sanctioned source is the staged archive, and only when its
sha256 matches the manifest checksum: the manifest is authority, the file on
disk is evidence, and filenames never decide identity.

WHAT THIS PINS. After a publish, every node can serve the artifact. The
seeding pass repeats for the life of the process rather than running once at
startup, so a node that loses its CAS mid-life heals without a restart.
